method.evidenceRule: Visible roof form and surface appearance may calibrate the renderer. Hidden layers, exact dimensions and construction joints remain unresolved until measured evidence is available.

lowerTier.centralProjectionCandidate: small front ridge or canopy element

visibleThickness.observation: Eave edges show a layered depth significantly greater than a single flat roof plate.

allowed: ridge and finial vocabulary for high-grade building classes
prohibited: automatic use on ordinary courtyard dwellings
copying decorative ridge pieces into Yikeyin houses
deriving exact tile or timber dimensions

mainRoof.ridge: long ridge with visible end lift and local curvature

secondaryRoofs.relation: lower side or rear roof masses attach or overlap below the main eave band
secondaryRoofs.junctionStatus: visible topology only, hidden flashing and valleys unresolved

tileAppearance.damageAndRepair: local irregularity visible but chronology unresolved

visibleThickness.observation: Eave edges, ridge caps and overlapping roof masses show separate depth bands.

allowed: small irregular eave and ridge curvature
prohibited: treating scan ground shards as roof fragments
treating the visible chimney candidate as a regional historical rule
inferring hidden valley, bedding or fastening details

roofSystem.courtyardRelation: roof masses enclose a central open void

tileRelationship.userConfirmed: Yunnan pan-tile and cover-tile visible relationship

allowed: visible pan-and-cover rhythm without dimensional claims
prohibited: using scan display scale as measured roof dimensions
treating 48 scan fragments as verified roofing components
copying exact laps or ridge closures from another case

roofHierarchy.finding: Yunnan reference buildings use several independent roof units and elevation bands. A single uniform roof shell loses the observed spatial hierarchy.

visibleRoofBuildUp.finding: Eave and ridge silhouettes require a layered visible thickness. The renderer must separate structural support, underlay placeholder, tile layer and edge closure.

roofColor.finding: Old gray tiles form a controlled cool-gray, warm-gray and brown-gray field with local highlights, stains and repairs. Uniform neutral gray is insufficient.

curvature.finding: Ridges and eaves show building-class-dependent curvature. High-grade Dali roof corners are strongly lifted, while dwelling roofs use subtler sag and lift.

damageAndRepair.finding: Missing edges, uneven rows, weathering and repair zones should be spatially controlled and sparse. Scan holes must remain excluded from authored damage.

colorFieldRules: Use deterministic seed per roof unit.
Keep one material-age family per roof unit.
Vary lightness, temperature and roughness within restrained ranges.
Apply distinct masks for ridge, eave, drainage, sheltered and repair zones.
Share the same color field across high, standard and distant quality levels.
roofGraphRules: Main house, side house, entrance block, gallery and auxiliary space retain independent roof-unit identities.
Roof intersections require an explicit junction type and evidence status.
Do not create automatic valleys where reference or measured evidence does not support them.
Do not merge staggered roofs into one continuous mesh for convenience.

qualityLevels.researchHigh: individual pan and cover tiles, explicit eave and ridge pieces, full color field
qualityLevels.webStandard: instanced tile courses with preserved IDs and full roof hierarchy
qualityLevels.distantSimplified: reduced geometry with the same roof graph, elevation bands and color field

unresolved: measured pan-tile and cover-tile longitudinal lap
ordinary dwelling eave and ridge closure details
measured ridge and eave elevations for Dali and Wulong cases
chronology and causes of visible repairs
qaRequirements: ridge and eave elevation bands are visible in top and oblique views
visible roof thickness contains more than one authored layer
tile color field is reproducible from seed
high and standard quality levels retain stable roof-unit and drainage IDs
large-angle rotation keeps correct depth occlusion
